response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT c.product_type_description AS d, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS aq, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) AS ad FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id JOIN Product_Categories c ON c.production_type_code = p.production_type_code GROUP BY c.product_type_description), m AS (SELECT AVG(ad) AS mad FROM cat) SELECT AVG(cat.aq) AS avg_quantity, AVG(cat.ad) AS avg_difference, AVG(cat.ad - m.mad) AS avg_excess FROM cat CROSS JOIN m WHERE cat.ad > m.mad;

assumptions.assumption: The difference is derived_product_cost minus derived_total_cost, following the order in the request. This is normally negative, because the total includes VAT.
product_quantity is stored as text, so it is cast to a number before averaging.

Categories are grouped by product_type_description, as the request says. The mean of all category averages is the unweighted mean across those groups. Categories whose average difference is NULL are left out of that mean.

alternatives.interpretation: The difference is derived_total_cost minus derived_product_cost, which is normally positive. This reverses the sign, so a different set of categories can pass the 'above the mean' filter.
